title: Assistant interruptibility & prioritization — notes and quick PRD sketch
content:
Quick brain-dump: exploring an "interruptibility" layer for assistant sessions. Goal is to let product-level signals (user interrupts, system alerts, urgent messages, high-priority background tasks) preempt or reshape in-flight generations without breaking UX or wasting large token budgets. This is a working sketch — lots of unknowns.

Context / why:
- Use cases: live chat where user edits prompt mid-generation; co-browsing assistants where server-side event (e.g., payment failed) needs immediate short notification; mobile push/low-bandwidth clients that need quick stump responses when connectivity flaps.
- Current problem: long generations are atomic; cancelling wastes compute/units and often results in confusing partial content. No consistent way to attach priority semantics to requests.

Design goals (top-level):
1) Fast graceful preemption: if higher-priority event arrives, we should be able to stop current gen and return an explainable partial response or a synthesized short stub.
2) Token-economy friendly: minimize double-spend (don't regenerate whole context repeatedly). Prefer techniques like delta continuation, trimmed restarts, or in-model short-circuiting.
3) Predictable UX: clients see stable states ("in-progress", "interrupted->short-retry", "completed-later") and get hooks for retry/backoff.
4) Policyable: product teams can define priority classes (USER_INTERACTION > SYSTEM_ALERT > BACKGROUND_SYNC) and tune allowed preemptions per class.

Proposed primitives (brainstorm):
- priority flag: integer enum (0..4) on every request; default 1 for normal.
- interruptable boolean: opt-in per route (to avoid unexpected partials for some APIs).
- preemption strategy: enum {RETURN_PARTIAL, SYNTHESIZE_SHORT_ACK, CANCEL_SILENT, FALLBACK_TO_SMALL_MODEL}.
- continuation token: opaque token to resume interrupted request cheaply (server-owned KV reference to KV-cache snapshot).

User stories (examples):
- As a chat user, I can press "stop" and immediately see a short summary/acknowledgement instead of a blank or stalled UI.
- As a mobile user with flaky LTE, the assistant will return a 1-sentence stub when connectivity degrades and resume full content when network is back.
- As product owner, I can mark a system alert as "critical" and ensure it preempts other background tasks.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Route-level opt-in for interruptibility exists in API schema.
- Server will accept preemption request and respond with one of: partial output + resume_token, short_ack, or cancel confirmation within 150ms of preemption call.
- Continuation resume reduces re-generated token count by >=30% vs naive restart (measurable in synthetic bench).
- Telemetry surfaces preemption events, preemption cause, time-to-respond, token impact, and percent resumed successfully.

Implementation notes / tech approaches to investigate:
- Serving runtime: leverage KV cache snapshotting per request (cheap metadata ref) so continuation can rehydrate quickly. Might need small refactor in cache lifecycle. (Talk to Serving Runtime team: Sana Iqbal.)
- Model-level: use control tokens or early-exit heads for short-ack generation (small auxiliary head that generates 8–16 token ack). Evaluate on 2B/7B/13B open models.
- Fallback models: maintain a tiny 1–2 layer distilled model (or tuned prompt) that can synthesize an ack quickly when preemption happens.
- Streaming semantics: for interrupted streamed responses we should send a final frame indicating "INTERRUPTED" + resume_token in metadata.

Telemetry and metrics to collect:
- preemptions_per_1k_requests, successful_resumes_pct, average_tokens_wasted_per_preempt, average_time_to_ack_ms, user_abort_via_ui_pct
- qualitative: sample interrupted responses and run micro-evals for coherence and user-perceived helpfulness.

Experiments (quick smoke tests):
- Synthetic bench: start 1k long-gen requests, preempt half at random times, compare token counts for naive restart vs continuation token resume.
- UX AB: client toggles interruptability; measure retention and click-to-stop rates.
- Model probes: small head vs fallback distilled model for ack generation — compare latency and semantic adequacy.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (prototype): run internal-only experiment on dev cluster; instrument heavy telemetry. (2–4 weeks)
- Phase 1 (alpha): expose to internal clients + a few pilot customers; default off; allow route opt-in (6–8 weeks)
- Phase 2 (beta): open to all hosted API clients; add console toggles, per-route UI; preemption cost insights in Optimize. (quarterly)

Risks / open questions:
- Security/privacy: resume tokens reference ephemeral KV states — ensure these are tenant-scoped and expire. Need to sync with Security + Privacy.
- Predictability: will partial outputs confuse users if not labeled clearly? Need clear client-side UX guidelines.
- Billing: how do we bill interrupted work vs resumed work? Might need to adjust billing rules to avoid double-charge perception. (Finance input required.)
- Hard preemption vs soft: some models might not support cheap preemption without large rewinds; must detect per-model capability and expose fallback.

TODOs / next steps (short list):
- [ ] Sync with Serving Runtime (Sana) on KV snapshot feasibility and cost.
- [ ] Rough latency/proof-of-concept using 7B distilled model for ack path. (Assign: Arjun)
- [ ] Draft API schema changes and migration notes (fields: priority, interruptable, preemption_strategy, resume_token).
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and link to this doc: JIRA-INT-1023 (placeholder).
- [ ] Quick UX sketch for stream termination frames and client indicators (Mira).

Notes to self: keep this opt-in per route initially. Avoid making cancellations default for long-tail legacy routes (email summaries, code generation). This is a cross-cutting feature touching runtime, billing, telemetry, and SDKs. Keep early experiments internal until we have a clean billing story.

Open questions for next sync:
1) Are there existing runtime hooks for snapshotting a per-request attention/KV state? cost estimate?
2) What is the minimum viable resume_token design that is secure and cheap? (opaque id -> short TTL)
3) If we synthesize a short_ack, should it be billed as an independent request or a modifier of the original?
4) Can we reuse existing fallback routing logic (model variant / small model) for preemption fallbacks?

If this lands in scope, potential nice-to-have later: priority-weighted batching (so high-priority items get preferential batching or dedicated lanes), UI-level "explain why preempted" field, and per-customer QoS quotas for preemptions.

End of sketch. Low-polish; share with Arjun + Mira for next sync.

-- kelly
